Services / Façade & high-access cleaning

Façade & high-access cleaning.

Façades and hard-to-reach areas cleaned with materials, access and surrounding activity considered together.

View the scope ↗

Match cleaning to the facade material.

We plan exterior cleaning around the actual surface and its condition. Glass, coated cladding, masonry and sheltered details do not all need the same method. We identify the areas, access and protection required, then agree the cleaning approach and water-control arrangements.

01 / Sheltered metal cladding junction

Identify the surface and what is on it

Map glass, coated metal and masonry separately and note flaking, existing cracks or sealant damage before washing. Where an agreed trial is appropriate, assess the result and runoff at a representative section before extending it to more elevations. Account for people below the work and openings that must remain usable.

We look at how adjacent materials meet, especially coated metal, glass, sealants and painted surfaces. A useful access plan covers the work face, the area beneath it and the route for water and equipment, with the cleaning method matched to the actual finish.

We compare rain-washed elevations with eaves, entry recesses and sheltered cladding. A visible deposit on a sound finish can be a cleaning item. Chalking, lifting coatings, opened joints and loose fixings are recorded separately for repair review. We verify the existing finish and product requirements, agree a suitable cleaning area and plan water, runoff and exclusion below.

  • Salt and deposited dirt

    We identify exposed and sheltered areas, including surfaces that receive little natural rain washing. For coated metal, the material and applicable product guidance inform the cleaning scope.

  • Stains or discolouration

    We assess the surface, coating and visible marks before selecting a method. The scope distinguishes removable soiling from existing deterioration or damage that requires a repair decision.

  • Joints, glazing and adjoining finishes

    We check accessible joints and neighbouring materials before work. Their condition affects protection and the suitability of a cleaning approach near openings or sensitive finishes.

02 / Facade elevations and access below

Agree the method after checking the material

  • A suitable trial area

    Where appropriate, we agree a small test area to review the cleaning result and surface response. Product, pressure and technique are selected for the material rather than assumed from the building height.

  • A realistic completion scope

    We identify the surfaces included and the treatment proposed for each. Staining that remains, damaged coating and defects revealed during cleaning are recorded separately from the completed cleaning tasks.

Prepare the site as carefully as the surface

Before scheduling a shopfront elevation, mark coating transitions and the paths below. The work brief should identify where the public can pass, where equipment can stand and which surfaces need a separate test or assessment.

  1. 01

    Confirm surfaces and access

    We identify the included elevations, substrate, existing condition and access restrictions, recording relevant defects before cleaning.

  2. 02

    Protect and clean

    We agree the work zone, protect adjacent glazing, landscaping and finishes, and use the specified method with the planned water arrangements.

  3. 03

    Review and hand back

    We review the cleaned areas against the scope, clear the agreed equipment and waste, and identify any follow-up repairs.

Water, pedestrians and trading belong in the brief

We discuss cleaning-water collection and disposal arrangements for the site, alongside entries, deliveries and public movement. The presence of a nearby drain does not by itself settle how cleaning wastewater should be managed. These arrangements are confirmed with the agreed method and work area.

What affects the quotation

  • Area and method

    Surface area, material sensitivity, soiling, test work and the extent of protection affect the cleaning allowance.

  • Access and staging

    Height, equipment positioning, ground access, water arrangements and trading restrictions affect attendance and staging. The quote states the agreed cleaning limits.

Close out cleaning and defects separately.

We identify cleaned areas, existing damage and any repair item that was outside the washing scope.

  • Materials and existing defects
  • Access and runoff plan
  • Cleaned areas and repair notes

Common questions

Is pressure washing suitable for every façade?
Check substrate, coating, joints and existing damage before setting the method. Base trial cleaning on guidance for the material.
Does façade cleaning include windows and sheltered areas?
The quotation names the included surfaces. Glazing, frames, undersides and sheltered details are identified separately where they form part of the agreed scope.
What happens if cleaning reveals a defect?
We record the location and visible condition for review. Any repair or different treatment outside the cleaning scope is separately defined before it proceeds.
